messages:
michael: Heads-up — canary for model 'redwood-open-7b-q4' is returning garbled outputs. Lots of repeated '<unk>' tokens and mid-sentence truncation. Observed right after deployment ~09:12 PST. Posting brief logs below.

jia: FYI weights + tokenizer path for this candidate are in S3: s3://redwood-models/onboard/open-7b/q4/sha256-abcdef. Can someone confirm which tokenizer the container is loading?

michael: In the running container tokenizer is at /app/models/tokenizer.json (48KB). But the canary logs contain repeated lines: "using byte fallback for missing token: 0xXX" — feels like vocab mismatch.

kevin: Did the model-registry manifest get updated? There was an earlier rename between tokenizer v1/v2. If config still points to an older tokenizer we could get silent fallbacks. Check model.config.json (vocab_size & merges).

jia: Quick check: model.config.json -> "vocab_size": 50304. tokenizer.json seems to have 50257 entries when I count. That's a mismatch.

andrew: That explains it — runtime didn't hard-fail, it fell back to byte-level tokenization for unknown ids which explodes token count. More tokens -> larger KV cache -> memory surge. We saw an OOM on the 4g canary node during load.

ops-bot: alert: pod redwood-canary-7b OOMKilled at 2026-03-17T09:14:23Z (container memory+swap exceeded).

dana: Immediate remediation: revert traffic to open-7b-vendored stable, mark this onboarding candidate blocked. Medium: either regenerate tokenizer to match weights or point config at the correct tokenizer artifact.

michael: I pushed a pointer fix in the model-registry manifest to tokenizer at s3://redwood-models/onboard/open-7b/v2/tokenizer.json — see PR #412. Can someone kick a quick canary (small instance) with that manifest?

kevin: Kicking canary now on an 8g node. Command I used: 
```
kubectl -n canary exec -it canary-deploy -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/predict -d @sample_prompt.json
```

jia: After forcing the corrected tokenizer, decoding looks normal — no <unk> spam or truncation. Peak memory during load ~6.2GB then stable. Will add a manifest validation step to compare declared vocab_size + tokenizer sha256 against the uploaded tokenizer.

andrew: Also adding a preflight tokenization check: run a standard prompt through candidate tokenizer and compare token count to baseline. If token count > baseline * 1.2, mark for manual review. That should catch tokenization blowups before canary.

michael: :thumbsup: Assigning manifest validation to Jia, Kevin to add canary infra checks. I'll draft a short doc in docs/onboarding for the runbook.

dana: Runbook note suggestion: if token mismatch detected, auto-label candidate 'needs-tokenizer', block canary, and fallback routing to previous stable variant. Saves us from noisy incidents.

kevin: I opened PRs: #413 adds the vocab_size/sha256 check in the registry CI; #414 adds the token-count preflight in canary infra. Will run tests and merge.

michael: Thanks everyone — reverting routing now and keeping this thread open until PRs merge. If it reappears, open an incident with logs and sample tokenization diffs.
